author: Good Enough
description:
Earth has experienced five catastrophic mass extinction events that nearly wiped out life on the planet. In this video we explore the 5 mass extinctions in Earth’s history, what the planet looked like during each era, the strange animals that lived at the time, and the disasters that caused these extinction events. The first event, the Ordovician extinction event, occurred about 444 million years ago when life was almost entirely confined to the oceans. Seas were filled with trilobites, brachiopods, and early reef systems, but a sudden global cooling and massive ice age caused sea levels to drop dramatically, wiping out much of marine life.

Millions of years later came the Late Devonian extinction, a prolonged series of extinction pulses around 372–359 million years ago.
